questions.prompt: What does a private endpoint do?

options.text: Gives a PaaS service a private IP inside your VNet so traffic avoids the public internet
Makes a storage account public to everyone
Assigns a role to a user

questions.explanation: A private endpoint is a network interface with a private IP in your VNet that connects privately (via Private Link) to a PaaS service, keeping traffic off the public internet.

questions.prompt: Which statements about VNet peering are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It connects two VNets so resources communicate over private IPs
Peered VNets must have non-overlapping address spaces
Peering is non-transitive (A-B and B-C does not connect A and C)
Peering only needs to be created on one of the two VNets

questions.explanation: Peering privately connects VNets, requires non-overlapping ranges, and is non-transitive. It must be created on both VNets to work.

questions.prompt: VNet peering is non-____, meaning peering A-B and B-C does not automatically connect A and C.
questions.explanation: Peering is non-transitive; you must connect A and C directly or use a hub-and-spoke design with routing.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to build and secure a subnet.

items.text: Associate the NSG with the subnet

questions.explanation: Create the VNet, carve a subnet, create an NSG with rules, then associate the NSG with the subnet.

questions.prompt: Match each networking concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: The private IP range a VNet owns
A subdivision of a VNet grouping resources
A private IP in your VNet for a PaaS service

questions.explanation: Address space is the VNet's IP range; subnets subdivide it; peering connects VNets; private endpoints give PaaS a private IP.
